notes.text: The Holy Ghost fell on all that were hearing the word — Thus were they consecrated to God, as the first fruits of the Gentiles. And thus did God give a clear and satisfactory evidence, that he had accepted them as well as the Jews.
The believers of the circumcision — The believing Jews.

Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Ghost? — He does not say they have the baptism of the Spirit; therefore they do not need baptism with water. But just the contrary: if they have received the Spirit, then baptize them with water. How easily is this question decided, if we will take the word of God for our rule! Either men have received the Holy Ghost or not. If they have not, Repent, saith God, and be baptized, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. If they have, if they are already baptized with the Holy Ghost, then who can forbid water?

In the name of the Lord — Which implies the Father who anointed him, and the Spirit with which he was anointed to his office. But as the Gentiles had before believed in God the Father, and could not but now believe in the Holy Ghost, under whose powerful influence they were at this very time, there was the less need of taking notice, that they were baptized into the belief and profession of the sacred Three: though doubtless the apostle administered the ordinances in that very form which Christ himself had prescribed.

glossa.text: *The Spirit.* The Spirit is the house of God, inasmuch as he is given to those who through him love God; but with himself he is God, even if he be given to none, coeternal with the Father and the Son. Nor, because they give, and he himself is given, is he less than they. For he is so given as the gift of God, that he gives himself as God: *For the Spirit breatheth where he will ((Joan. III))*.
*Can any man forbid water,* etc. As if, God first gave what is greater, and inverted the order, can he forbid what is less You have come for this, that you may be witnesses, therefore judge.

*In the name of Christ.* Whereas the rule of the Church is that baptism be delivered in the name of the Trinity, Luke nevertheless testifies that it was given in the name of Jesus Christ. Ambrose, resolving this, says that through the unity of the name the mystery is made full, because he who says Christ designates also the Father, from whom the Son is, and the Holy Spirit: he also who says the Father shows alike both the Son and the Spirit: and he who names the Spirit calls also the Father, from whom the Spirit proceeds, and the Son, whose Spirit he also is. Whence, that authority may be joined to reason, one is baptized also in the Spirit, according to that: *But you shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit ((Act. XI))*, and the Apostle: *In one Spirit we have been baptized ((I Cor. XII))*.

notes.text: Salvation — The redemption of the world by the Messiah: which was hitherto reserved was a secret among the Jews, yea was not throughly known by the most of the Jews themselves. Righteousness - His faithfulness in accomplishing this great promise. Israel is required to praise God, for their hasty constitution both in church and state, ver. 1-5. Some instances of the happy administration of it, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text:
*Sing ye to the Lord.* ((CASS.)) First he speaks of the showing forth of the saving right hand.

*He hath saved.* ((AUG.)) It is a greater thing that he raised up the whole world from eternal death, than that he raised the dead. *To himself.* Many are saved bodily, but to themselves, not to him: they who, having received bodily health, grow wanton, but they who by faith are healed within, are healed to him, or save themselves.

*Salvation . . . justice.* ((AUG.)) He who saves and justifies. *He hath revealed.* Things to come were foretold under a veil by the prophets: but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth.*

*Of mercy and of truth.* ((AUG.)) *Mercy* is that whereby he promised, *truth* follows upon this, because he rendered it. But to whom? *To Israel,* that is, to him who now by faith sees the truth, afterwards by sight.
*All.* ((ID.)) Because Christ was not given to certain men only.
*Rejoice ye.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he says that in all ways he is to be praised and declared, because the judge is come.

*With ductile trumpets and with the voice of a trumpet of horn.* ((AUG.)) Of brass, which are drawn out by beating, etc., *as far as* as the horn cleaves to the flesh, and surpasses it. ((HIERON.)) With ductile trumpets, of silver, after the manner of the Jews. Mystically, drawn out under the hammer of the whole earth, that is, the devil. ((AUG.)) Tribulation is the beating; advancement, the drawing out: such a trumpet was Job, whence he sounded as a trumpet, saying: *The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away.*

*Let it be moved.* ((ID.)) That is, let the sea of the law be made sweet, the wood of the cross being set therein. *And the fulness thereof.* All the sacraments of the law, etc., *as far as* but *the rivers,* etc. *The earth.* ((CASS.)) That is, every sinner.

*The world of the earth.* All earthly men. *In justice.* ((AUG.)) Because they did not merit mercy. *The peoples.* ((CASS.)) The faithful out of the Jews and the Gentiles, who shall receive things equal to their merits.

notes.text: The scope and sum of this whole paragraph appears from the conclusion of it, 1 John v, xiii, "These things have I written to you who believe, that ye may know that ye who believe have eternal life." So faith is the first and last point with St. John also. Every one who loveth — God that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him - Hath a natural affection to all his brethren.
Hereby we know — This is a plain proof. That we love the children of God - As his children.
For this is the love of God — The only sure proof of it. That we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous - To any that are born of God.

For whatsoever — This expression implies the most unlimited universality. Is born of God overcometh the world - Conquers whatever it can lay in the way, either to allure or fright the children of God from keeping his commandments. And this is the victory - The grand means of overcoming. Even our faith - Seeing all things are possible to him that believeth.

Who is he that overcometh the world — That is superior to all worldly care, desire, fear? Every believer, and none else. The seventh verse (usually so reckoned) is a brief recapitulation of all which has been before advanced concerning the Father, the Son, and the Spirit. It is cited, in conjunction with the sixth and eighth, 1 John v, 6, 8 by Tertullian, Cyprian, and an uninterrupted train of Fathers. And, indeed, what the sun is in the world, what the heart is in a man, what the needle is in the mariner's compass, this verse is in the epistle. By this the sixth, eighth, and ninth verses 1 John v, 6, 8, 9 are indissolubly connected; as will be evident, beyond all contradiction, when they are accurately considered.

This is he — St. John here shows the immovable foundation of that faith that Jesus is the Son of God; not only the testimony of man, but the firm, indubitable testimony of God. Who came - Jesus is he of whom it was promised that he should come; and who accordingly, is come. And this the Spirit, and the water, and the blood testify. Even Jesus - Who, coming by water and blood, is by this very thing demonstrated to be the Christ. Not by the water only - Wherein he was baptized. But by the water and the blood - Which he shed when he had finished the work his Father had given him to do. He not only undertook at his baptism "to fulfil all righteousness," but on the cross accomplished what he had undertaken; in token whereof, when all was finished, blood and water came out of his side. And it is the Spirit who likewise testifieth - Of Jesus Christ, namely, by Moses and all the prophets, by John the Baptist, by all the apostles, and in all the writings of the New Testament. And against his testimony there can be no exception, because the Spirit is truth - The very God of truth.

glossa.text: *Every one that believeth.* He believes who so lives as Christ commanded, otherwise the devils also believe. But works apart from faith are either nothing, or, even if they seem good, are empty, because they are apart from the way, which is Christ. Truly he who loves God loves his brother. For he who loves God the Father loves God the Son, begotten of the Father, and he who loves God the Son loves also the sons of God, the members of that head.

*They are not heavy. ((BEDA.))* They do not draw downward, like a talent of lead, etc., *as far as* lest anyone should trust that by his own strength he can overcome the world, he adds concerning faith:
*And this is the victory,* etc. That faith, namely, which works through love, which craves God's help.

*But who is he?* etc. He determines what faith conquers, namely the faith of Christ. As if to say: Truly through faith he conquers the world, because through anything else it is not conquered. *Our faith.* Behold what faith conquers, that which believes him true man and true God.

*This is he,* etc. Because faith and the confession of the divinity alone does not suffice for salvation and for overcoming the world, he adds also concerning the humanity: therefore he expressed the blood.

*The spirit.* That is, the human soul which he gave up in the passion; *water and blood,* which flowed from his side. This could not have been done, if he had not had the true nature of flesh. But even before the passion, the sweat which was made like drops of blood showed the truth of the flesh. And this, that from the side of one already dead, against nature, water, blood flowed vigorously, bore witness that the body of the Lord would live better after death, and that his death would give us life. But that the sweat flowed like blood onto the earth signified that he would wash the Church in the whole world with his own blood.

notes.text: Abide ye in my love — Keep your place in my affection. See that ye do not forfeit that invaluable blessing. How needless a caution, if it were impossible for them not to abide therein?
If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love — On these terms, and no other, ye shall remain the objects of my special affection.
That my joy might remain in you — The same joy which I feel in loving the Father, and keeping his commandments.
Your joy will be full, if ye so love one another.
Greater love — To his friends. He here speaks of them only.
Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you — On this condition, not otherwise. A thunderbolt for Antinomianism! Who then dares assert that God's love does not at all depend on man's works?
All things — Which might be of service to you.

Ye — My apostles, have not chosen me, but I have chosen you - As clearly appears from the sacred history: and appointed you, that ye may go and bear fruit - I have chosen and appointed you for this end, that ye may go and convert sinners: and that your fruit may remain - That the fruit of your labours may remain to the end of the world; yea, to eternity; that whatsoever ye shall ask - The consequence of your going and bearing fruit will be, that all your prayers will be heard.

glossa.text: *That joy.* The joy of God concerning us, whom he foreknew and predestined, is always full; in us it begins from faith, it grows, nay and shall be perfected in the resurrection.

*This is the commandment,* etc. And above concerning love toward the neighbour; but repetition is confirmation: there, however, he says, I give a commandment, as though it had not been before; but here, this is, as though it were not another. There, New, lest we remain in oldness; here, Mine, lest it be contemned.
*Greater than this.* He defines the fulness of mutual love which he commands them to have.

*Now I will not call.* Love having been commended, he adds what belongs to condescension, that he should call good servants (who know by doing the things he commands) friends, and takes from them the name of servant, which is from fear, by casting it out, [the servant] who does not know what his Lord does. Because when he does anything, he is so exalted as though he himself did it, and not the lord.

*These things I command,* etc. Here he shows what is the fruit of which he had spoken, for which the Father will also give what we ask, who gave this also, that we should love.

*That you love one another. ((AUG.))* Deservedly does he often commend love, as though it alone were to be commanded, without which the rest cannot be, and which without the rest cannot be had. And for its sake we ought patiently to endure even all the adversities of the world. Whence he subjoins:

registers.label: Spare
lines: Abide in my love, the Lord says.
As the Father has loved me, so I love you.
You are no longer servants but friends.
He has called us friends.
Love one another as I have loved you.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Sing to the Lord a new song. Come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Sing something new this morning, you whom God has chosen, for the old griefs do not get the last word.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He no longer calls you servant, kept at arm's length; he calls you friend, and tells you everything.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He says, Abide in my love, and let my joy be in you, and let your joy be full.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
So love one another the way he first loved you, and watch the Spirit fall on every kind of person.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

lines: Sing to the Lord a new song.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He calls us friends and tells us all he knows.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Abide in his love; let your joy be full.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Come, let us love as we are loved.
We are his friends. Alleluia!
